🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin is holding near $84K as the market digests Bitget's $387M hack fallout, while U.S. regulators and courts keep reshaping crypto rules with Congress sidelined. 🚨 Bitget Sets Withdrawal Restart After $387.5M Hack Bitget says the exploit behind its September 24 breach is found and patched, and withdrawals will reopen in stages: bitcoin on September 28, ether on September 29, USDT on September 30, and remaining tokens, fiat and P2P by October 2. The exchange has raised its loss estimate to $387.5 million after tracing Zcash and TRON transfers, offers a 5% recovery bounty, and its CEO says North Korean hackers are suspected. Read full story 👋 SEC's "Crypto Mom" Hester Peirce to Exit October 2 SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce, the agency's most consistent crypto advocate and head of its crypto task force, confirmed her long-expected departure next week. The announcement landed alongside fresh crypto policy guidance from the agency. More details 📜 SEC and CFTC Issue New Crypto Guidance SEC staff published an FAQ on token buybacks, network upgrades and marketing, saying that promoting a network's current uses generally does not create an expectation of profit. The CFTC separately said futures firms may invest customer funds in tokenized versions of permitted assets and may keep required records onchain, provided they can always produce them. Both moves come as the Clarity Act remains stalled in the Senate. Read more ⚖️ Sixth Circuit Rules Against Kalshi on Sports Contracts A unanimous Sixth Circuit panel found Kalshi's sports event contracts are not swaps and that federal commodities law does not block Ohio and Tennessee from enforcing their gambling laws. It is the second appellate loss for the prediction market, deepening a circuit split that makes Supreme Court review increasingly likely. See details 🏦 Strategy Proposes Daily Dividends on Preferred Stock Strategy wants STRC, STRF, STRK and STRD to pay dividends daily, with every calendar day becoming a record date, subject to a shareholder vote on October 28.
